content: The interaction between magnesium oxide and anhydrous citric acid can lead to an increase in the toxicity of either compound. This interaction may result in fluid and electrolyte imbalances. It is recommended to use caution and monitor the patient closely. Dicloxacillin reduces the effectiveness of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid by altering their metabolism. Coadministration with antibiotics can decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by disrupting colonic bacterial flora, which is necessary for converting sodium picosulfate into its active form. Caution and monitoring are advised. Diflunisal, when combined with sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid, can increase the toxicity of either agent.
